hints: Focus on how atomic radius changes across Period 3 from Na to Ar, and remember the noble gas is a special case.
Deduction / Stepping Stone: D must be chlorine, as it is the smallest atom that forms a normal covalent radius in Period 3.
Synthesis / Final Link: List Period 3 melting points from lowest up, find the element with exactly two elements below it, then check which pair can combine to give one of the listed formulas.
walkthrough:
**Identify element D from atomic radius**

Think left to right across a period. More protons pull the same shells in tighter, so radius gets smaller.

Trend across Period 3: $\text{Na} > \text{Mg} > \text{Al} > \text{Si} > \text{P} > \text{S} > \text{Cl}$

**Remember the argon exception**

Argon does not form covalent bonds, so we use its much larger van der Waals radius. For exam purposes, the smallest covalent radius is chlorine.

So: $\text{D} = \text{Cl}$

**Identify element E from melting point**

Recall the melting point pattern. Giant covalent Si is highest, then metals Mg and Al, then the rest are low.

Lowest values are roughly: $\text{Ar } (-189^\circ\text{C}) < \text{Cl } (-101^\circ\text{C}) < \text{P } (44^\circ\text{C}) < \text{Na } (98^\circ\text{C}) < \text{S } (113^\circ\text{C})$

**Count two elements lower than E**

We need the element with exactly two Period 3 elements below it. That is the third lowest.

That gives: $\text{E} = \text{P}$, since only Ar and Cl are lower.

**Combine D and E to make L**

We have $\text{Cl}$ + $\text{P}$ reacting together. Phosphorus forms covalent chlorides such as $\text{PCl}_3$.

Compound L: $$\text{P} + \text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3$$

options.A: MgCl2 needs Mg and Cl. Cl is correct for D, but Mg is not E. Mg has a high melting point near 650 C with five elements lower than it, not two.
options.B: MgS needs Mg and S. Neither fits. Mg is not the smallest atom and S does not have exactly two elements with lower melting point.
options.C: Na2S needs Na and S. Na is the largest atom in Period 3, not the smallest, and Na has three elements (Ar, Cl, P) with lower melting point, not two.
options.D: PCl3 needs P and Cl. This fits perfectly. Cl has the smallest covalent radius in Period 3, and P has exactly two elements (Ar and Cl) with a lower melting point.
